McCoy, All Rights Reserved.'; (2) 'You are not authorized to modify, retype, translate, copy or otherwise duplicate the Questionnaire except with the further and prior written permission of Mapi Research Trust / the developers / copyright holders / distributors.'; (3) for funded academic, healthcare and commercial users, 'Fees may apply to your project ... license agreement'. Under the irw#1945 reserve-a-right test (permission-required, no-derivatives/no-copy, fee) this blocks, and under the 2026-09-04 DSES/WHOQOL generalisation the holder's clause outranks the source deposit's licence - so the fact that IRW's copy would have come from the CC BY PLOS deposit's own SPSS value labels does not save it. A Dutch translation was administered; a translation is a derivative of the restricted instrument and is covered by the same clause. WHAT WOULD HAVE SHIPPED, had rights allowed: the S2 File .sav (journal.pone.0205934.s002) carries per-item VALUE labels giving each item's 1/4/7 anchors (e.g. MCC4 1='Not at all exited', 4='Moderately exited', 7='Extremely exited'; MCC9/MCC17/MCC18/MCC19 reverse-anchored 1='Every time' .. 7='Never'), with levels 2,3,5,6 unlabelled. Its VARIABLE labels are bare ('McCoy Q1 - Follow-up'), so item stems are NOT in the deposit and the paper does not reproduce them; even absent the rights bar this would have been an option-only table under the #1770 rule. The block does reach something: the IRW item codes are MCC1..MCC19 and carry no wording, so no MFSQ text is exposed by the response table. RETRY TEST: NO - determinate. The licence reserves rights; an unchanged retry now returns the same page and the same clauses. It would flip only if the copyright holder or Mapi Research Trust published the MFSQ under terms that reserve nothing, or if Ben ruled the clause inapplicable.

note: Item wording transcribed literally from the paper's Table 1, which is a table IMAGE -- no text route reaches it, so the transcription is manual from the PNG and is worth a spot-check; the paper's own grammatical slip in confi4 ('you will always someone around you caring about you') and character4's lone trailing period are reproduced as printed. Table 1 groups items by subscale and gives a factor loading for each but prints NO item code, so the code-to-text tie is presentation order within each subscale: mapping_basis=paper_order, checked against the data per verification_wen_2022_pyd.csv (all 26 loadings reproduce to <=0.0052; 20 of 26 items uniquely pinned). The processing script data/wen_2022_pyd.py derives each IRW code by stripping a fixed 'PYD_' prefix from the .sav column name, a mechanical rename, so no positional assignment is involved; the .sav variable labels are original questionnaire codes (P2Q4S01 etc.), not item text, which is why they settle ordering but not wording. Administered in Chinese to Beijing and Anhui seventh-graders; no Chinese wording exists anywhere in the deposit -- the only supplements are S1/S2 Data (.sav; s003-s005 return 404), and their only CJK strings are the labels for the smoke/drink covariates, none for the 26 PYD variables and no value labels on them at all. So the fallback applies: the authors' own published English sits in the base fields, language=Chinese, the _translated columns are empty. option_text is blank throughout and that is deliberate: neither the paper nor the .sav discloses the 1-5 anchors, and the anchors visibly differ by item (self-ratings of health, confidence ratings, and agreement statements are mixed in one table), so there is nothing to transcribe and the scale points were not padded with their own numbers. Rights: the scale was developed by these authors and first published in this CC BY 4.0 article; no fee, permission, non-commercial, no-derivatives or no-redistribution clause was found, and no register row applies.
public_note: Item wording is the authors' own published English; respondents read a Chinese questionnaire whose wording the study never deposited, and the 1-5 response anchors are not published anywhere, so option_text is blank.
